clue.text: Seaman struck North Sea oil, working

indicators.note: struck suggests the letters being knocked about and set down anew

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A sailor strikes it rich with a North Sea oil find that is up and running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' is the anagram signal: the letters of NORTH SEA OIL rearrange to HORATIONELS, and ON (working) completes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's most famous admiral, the victor of Trafalgar, is the seaman of all seamen.

clue.text: Hard, long thumb

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A tough, lengthy thumb, described in a few words.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a lift is to hitch one, flagging cars at the roadside.

clue.text: Form of choir — sad, subdued by Pastor? On the contrary

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Form of choir — sad, subdued by Pastor? On the contrary', is all wordplay (anagram of CHOIR SAD around P): no word defines RHAPSODIC, and 'Pastor' as P is unexplained; likely OCR loss of the definition.
annotationWithheld.clue: Form of choir — sad, subdued by Pastor? On the contrary

clue.text: Some accompanied Arthur, picking up second-hand car?

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up lifts the letters, so they read from the bottom upwards
some of the letters of the following words are taken, not all of them

explanation.surface: A knight who rode alongside King Arthur takes on a used car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes NIEDART from accompaNIED ARThur, and 'picking up' turns it upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A car handed over in part exchange becomes a used vehicle on the dealer's forecourt.

clue.text: Like 1 Across, outlaws gambling games

parts.note: the admiral of 1 Across lost his right arm at Santa Cruz in 1797
outlaws are bandits

explanation.surface: Outlaws who share a sailor's disability are playing games of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference leans on Nelson having only one arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Slot machines are nicknamed for their single lever and their habit of robbing players.

clue.text: It's stretched back in lace pants

indicators.note: pants as a verb in British slang means to make a poor job of something, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: the letters of it's, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment's waistband has been pulled back inside some lacy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but is the anagram signal for IT'S plus LACE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Material that springs back to its original shape after being pulled out is resilient in this way.

clue.text: Peter out chasing Army girl

indicators.note: chasing means the following piece comes after the other one

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
to peter out is to fade away or die

explanation.surface: Peter runs off after a girl serving in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name but 'Peter out' is one phrase meaning die.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, a short form of Sarah.

clue.text: Aussie soap character Robin's joining huge cast?

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Robin, the possessive giving none
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor named Robin joins the enormous cast of an Australian soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' fits the soap-opera picture but is the anagram signal for ROBIN plus HUGE. Neighbours is a long-running Australian TV soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone living on Ramsay Street in the Australian serial is one of its title residents.

clue.text: Stake taken back, seeing volatile mount

indicators.note: taken back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: A gambler's stake is withdrawn on seeing an unpredictable horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily's active volcano is a mountain liable to erupt.

clue.text: Pope loses bearing, knocking back first-class Mediterranean

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the pope's name

parts.note: Alexander was the name of several popes
E, east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: knocking back reverses the letters of the first-class term

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: A pope loses his way and knocks back a first-rate drink by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping E from ALEXANDER gives ALEXANDR; 'knocking back' turns AI (A1) into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt's great port city lies on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Sort of sauce involving herbs, evenly chopped?

definitions.text: Sort of sauce involving herbs, evenly chopped?

indicators.note: sort as a verb, to arrange, so the letters are rearranged
the even-placed letters of herbs are chopped off, leaving its odd ones

explanation.surface: A cook describes a sauce full of finely chopped herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly chopped' removes E and B from herbs, leaving HRS; 'Sort of' rearranges SAUCE plus HRS. 'involving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunter's sauce of mushrooms, wine and herbs such as tarragon and parsley.

clue.text: Fell hard squeezing through to rock

indicators.note: squeezing through means being pushed inside that word

parts.note: tho is an informal short spelling of though, here standing for through
to fell a tree is to hew it

explanation.surface: A climber falls heavily while squeezing through a gap in the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' is the music, not stone: the band are rock legends.
explanation.definitionFit: The British band of 'My Generation' are a classic rock group.

clue.text: 400m man concentrated by perimeter in college strip

indicators.note: concentrated by means the man is gathered right up against the next piece

parts.note: one lap of a standard athletics track is 400 metres
Dan is a man's name

indicators.note: the perimeter of the word college is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A college runner who completes a 400m lap finally strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: The perimeter of college is its first and last letters, C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic dance performed close up to a seated customer is a kind of striptease.

clue.text: Everyone welcomes break in ramble-is it activated by stirring tea leaves?

definitions.text: it activated by stirring tea leaves?

indicators.note: welcomes means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: break in suggests the word ramble is broken up and reset

explanation.surface: Everyone takes a break in the middle of a long walk for a cup of stirred tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea leaves' is rhyming slang: tea leaf means thief, so stirring tea leaves are burglars on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar alarm rings when an intruder starts to move about.

clue.text: Players love Ronaldo's heading — he's a star

parts.note: the players in a play are its cast
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the heading of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Teammates adore Ronaldo's header: he is a football superstar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' looks like Ronaldo's header but takes the first letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the twin stars of Gemini shares its name with the mythical brother of Pollux.

clue.text: Not socially acceptable to overpower a criminal clergyman

indicators.note: not means the socially acceptable letter is taken away

parts.note: to overpower someone is to subdue them
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, as opposed to non-U
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: It's bad form to overpower a crook who is a member of the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not socially acceptable' looks like one phrase meaning rude; here it removes U from SUBDUE, giving SUBDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor cleric ranking just below a deacon.

clue.text: It could get you first place in many a racecourse

definitions.text: It could get you first place in many a racecourse

indicators.note: first place in means the opening letter of many

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A lucky charm might win you a race at many a course.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a racecourse near Windsor, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's lucky charm is supposed to bring it victory.

clue.text: Restaurant worker turns up, overcoming hail and thunder, finally

indicators.note: overcoming means sitting over, so around in a down clue
in a down clue turns up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a worker is an ant
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of thunder

explanation.surface: A restaurant worker arrives after braving hail and thunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reads the worker upwards in this down entry, and 'overcoming' wraps it round the rest; 'and' is a link. 'hail and thunder' looks like weather but gives a greeting plus a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek eating place is a taverna.

clue.text: Type of malnutrition — spitting out fruit, needing a brace

indicators.note: a brace is a pair, so the sound is needed twice
spitting out words is saying them, so the fruit is heard

parts.note: a berry is a fruit

explanation.surface: A child refuses fruit and has to wear dental braces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spitting out' says BERRY aloud as BERI, and 'needing a brace' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease caused by lack of thiamine, vitamin B1, is a deficiency disorder.

clue.text: Coffee bars to relocate around university

indicators.note: around means the anagram is placed round the U
to relocate is to move, so the letters move to new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coffee bars are moving out to be near the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocate' rearranges the fodder 'bars to'; it is not a link word, and its letters go round the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy variety of coffee bean grown widely in Africa and Vietnam.

clue.text: Member in ballet 19 centre missing first ad-lib performance, 21 briefly

indicators.note: in means the member sits inside the other piece
missing first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the Kirov in St Petersburg is a famous centre of ballet
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician in a ballet company misses the first act of an unscripted show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing first' drops K from KIROV, leaving IROV, which MP goes into. 'briefly' says the answer is a shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for improvisation, theatre made up on the spot.

clue.text: Find new home for nursery item one's smashed up?

definitions.text: Find new home for nursery item

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker, one who is smashed

explanation.surface: A child's toy is rehoused after being broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' is a plant nursery, not a child's room: the item is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant outgrowing its container is moved into a larger one.

clue.text: Boxing watery-eyed punching back heavyweight?

indicators.note: punching means driving into the other piece
back means the weight's letters are reversed

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
blear eyes are watery and dim

explanation.surface: A tearful heavyweight boxer throws a punch in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavyweight' looks like a boxer but is a weight of a ton; 'back' reverses it and 'punching' drives the watery-eyed word in, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing has long been called the sport of fist-fighting with gentlemanly rules.

clue.text: European streets maintaining law, principally, need them

definitions.text: European streets maintaining law, principally, need them

indicators.note: maintaining means holding the other piece within

parts.note: rues are French streets

indicators.note: principally takes the first letter of law

explanation.surface: Cities across Europe need regulations to keep order in their streets.
explanation.walkthrough: RUES holds L, the first letter of law.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulations are what keep streets and law in order.

clue.text: Female flings her panties in the air

indicators.note: letters thrown in the air land in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman throws her underwear up in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flings' looks like a verb but is the noun: parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrations for a bride-to-be and her friends before the wedding.

clue.text: Young creature quiet with the opposite sex

indicators.note: male M is swapped for female F

parts.note: quiet means calm

explanation.surface: A young animal is subdued in the company of the other sex.
explanation.walkthrough: M (male) in CALM becomes F (female).
explanation.definitionFit: A baby cow is a young animal.

clue.text: Raunchy shantyman's tale lifting a Northern seaside community

indicators.note: raunchy suggests something rough and wild, so the letters are shaken up
lifting means stealing away the letter A from the pool

explanation.surface: A sailor's bawdy song is lifted by a northern seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: SHANTYMANSTALE less A rearranges to the town. Lytham St Annes is a seaside resort in Lancashire, near Blackpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lancashire resort town on the coast of north-west England.
